chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Sa'id al-Mukari, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I buy food and measure it (by volume), and with me is someone who has witnessed the measuring, and I am only measuring it for myself. Then he says to me: 'Sell it to me,' so I sell it to him for that same measure that I measured. He said: 'There is no harm (in it).'

key_terms.الْكَيْل: Measuring by volume (e.g., using a container like a sa' or mud)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell food measured by volume if you measured it yourself?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling on selling *al-madmun* (goods under one's control) by establishing that self-measurement is valid when accompanied by a witness, thereby preventing disputes over quantity. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the presence of a witness (*shahid*) suffices to ensure transparency and trustworthiness in commercial transactions involving bulk goods. This ruling facilitates trade by reducing the need for third-party measurement while maintaining the integrity of the contract.
